paper.title: No-regret learning for repeated non-cooperative games with lossy bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated concave N-player game with lossy bandit feedback (per-player regret)
unmapped: Non-cooperative N-player game: player i's utility u_i(a_i, a_{-i}) is concave in own action with L_i-Lipschitz partial gradient; other players also run the same algorithm (extras multi_agent_cooperative is only an approximation: players are non-cooperative)
Lossy bandit feedback: each round player i receives its utility value only with probability p_i (i.i.d. Bernoulli), otherwise keeps action unchanged
Step-size uses known reception probability p_i
Utility maximization, utilities bounded by compactness (not normalised to [0,1])
Learner needs a safety ball B_{r_i}(c_i) inside its action set
settings.definition_quote: Reg^{(i)}(K)=max_{a_i' in A_i} { sum_{k=1}^K u_i(a_i', a_{-i,k}) - sum_{k=1}^K u_i(a_{i,k}, a_{-i,k}) }. Let p_i denote the probability that player i will receive its utility value, then the probability of information loss is 1-p_i.

settings.name_in_paper: Beta-strongly monotone game with lossy bandits (Nash equilibrium convergence)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Game-theoretic equilibrium convergence result (mean-square distance to Nash equilibrium), not a regret guarantee
unmapped: Objective: mean-square convergence of action profile to Nash equilibrium
Lossy bandit feedback with known probability p_i
settings.definition_quote: Suppose that G is a beta-strongly monotone game on action space A, i.e., <g(a)-g(a'), a-a'> <= -beta ||a-a'||^2

source.label: regret
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with step-size $\gamma_{i,k}=\gamma_{k}p_{i}^{-w}$ and constant $w>0$. Suppose that $\{\gamma_{k}\}$ and $\{\delta_{k}\}$ are non-increasing sequences with $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then for each $i$, E[Reg^{(i)}(K)] <= p_i^{w-1}B_i^2/(2\gamma_K) + \sum_k B_iL_i\sqrt{N}\delta_k + \sum_k p_i^{w-1}/(2\gamma_k) G_i^2/\delta_k^2 E[\gamma_{i,k}^2]

results.notes: Since gamma_{i,k} is deterministic, E[gamma_{i,k}^2]=gamma_k^2 p_i^{-2w} was substituted. Regret is measured at intended actions a_{i,k}, not applied (perturbed) actions. K in paper is horizon T. The ontology mapping (convex body, adaptive adversary) is approximate: opponents run the same algorithm.

source.label: no-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1-2 hold. Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with $\gamma_{i,k}=1/(k^{b}p_{i})$ and $\delta_{k}={\delta_{1}}k^{-c}$ with $0<b<1$, $0<c<b/2$ and $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then for each $i$, E[Reg^{(i)}(K)] <= \frac{B_{i}^{2}}{2}k^{b} + ...

results.notes: Paper writes k^b in the first term, clearly meaning K^b (horizon). c is mapped to c_alg. Remark following gives O(K^{max{b,1-c,1-b+2c}}), e.g. K^{3/4} for b=3/4, c=1/4.

symbols.beta_mon: strong monotonicity parameter of the game

conditions: u_i concave and C^1 in a_i, partial gradient Lipschitz

source.label: the2
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1, 2, and 5 hold. Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with $\gamma_{i,k}={1}/({k p_{i}})$ and $\delta_{k}={\delta_{1}}k^{-1/3}$ with $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then $$\mathbb{E}\left[\|\hat{a}_{k}-a^{*}\|^{2} \right] =\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2\min\{\beta, 1/6\}}\right).$$

results.notes: Bound on mean-square distance of the applied action profile at iteration k (here T) to the Nash equilibrium, not a regret. Theorems 2 and 4 (almost-sure convergence to Nash, known/unknown p_i) are qualitative and not recorded.
